title: Code-review radar for interviews
hook: Interviewers do not want a compiler. They want the order you notice danger. This page is that order, citing the modules behind it.

sections.heading: Pass 1: lifetime and asynchrony
sections.prose: Look for `IDisposable` that never got `using` — SkiaSharp, `HttpClient` misuse, `IMemoryOwner` (modules 06 and 17). Look for `async void` except event handlers, discarded `Task`s on an SQS handler, and `lock` around `await` (modules 13 and 15). Look for `Span` stored on a field or used after `await` (module 17). Look for `fixed` pointers that escape the block. If the snippet is a consumer, ask where cancellation token flows. This pass finds production outages. Style can wait.

snippets.label: Radar hits in one method
snippets.explanation: Call out: no CancellationToken, possible null dto, shared mutable cache, deserialize allocating on a hot path. Do not start with “Id should be camelCase.”

sections.heading: Pass 2: allocations and closed world
sections.prose: CSV `Split`, LINQ `ToList` on a hot path already enumerated (module 12), `+` string loops instead of `string.Create`/`TryWrite`, reflection `GetTypes` on each message (module 16), extra DTO clones (previous topic). Ask whether Native AOT is in play (module 01). If yes, string-named `GetMethod` is a trim bug, not a style nit. Prefer a generated dispatcher. High-concurrency attempt-submit (199 → 999) makes these nits into incidents.

sections.heading: Pass 3: surface, then style
sections.prose: New `public` on a library without PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt (module 16) is a contract change. `InternalsVisibleTo` missing so someone made the parser public. `[Obsolete]` without a replacement. Then naming: `_` vs `s_`, interface `I`, record properties PascalCase (identifier-names). Then language-version toys used for no reason: interceptors, unexplained `unsafe`, `dynamic`. In a live interview, say the pass number. It shows you will not bikeshed while a native handle leaks. Tie the recap together: C# 8–14 (this module) is how you date a construct; modules 14–17 are how you decide if it is safe at run time.

interviewTakeaways: Review lifetime and async before allocations, public API, and naming.
Cite module-level rules (Span, Dispose, InternalsVisibleTo) instead of vague “best practices.”
Treat unapproved public surface as a product bug, not a formatter issue.
commonPitfalls: Spending the interview on brace style while async void ships.
Demanding Span in a once-a-day admin tool — wrong pass, wrong intensity.
Failing to mention CI public API files when the prompt is a shared library PR.

jsTsCorrelations.note: A senior Node review also starts with resource leaks (streams) and unhandled promises, then allocations, then exports. The C#-specific radar is pinning, ref structs, and assembly public surface.
